She has suggested that on the return of her brother-in-law
Smith should be given some remuneration for
writing the Life of her late husband. Smith is very
hurt and indignant at this suggestion and protests that
he wrote and printed the book at his own cost solely to
show the world the excellence of her husband in wisdom,
piety arid learning and was inspired to do so by the
great love and friendship he had for him. Has sent a
copy to the Royal Society. The work is praised by Lord
Clarendon and the Archbp: of Armagh.

victorys in Germany. "You may easily imagine that
the D. of M. will have no inconsiderable part in the

docs.dcterms_abstract:
He reports Lord Compton's progress under doses of physick to his
stomach, and the doctor's visit. "It worked his Lordship eight
times". His Lordship presents his duty to My Lord and to your
Ladyship and his services to all the Ladies; and returns his Papa
thanks for his letter.

docs.dcterms_abstract:
My Lord Compton has had another purge with milder effect. He has
given My Lord's summer coat and breeches to Mr. Herne to lengthen,
and he will need some more worsted and more thread stockings.
